verdict.rationale: Cursor is driven by plain-language prompts. The CLI agent takes natural-language instructions to write, review and modify code (e.g. `agent -p "Add comprehensive JSDoc comments..."`), and the `/automate` skill lets users describe a workflow in plain language while Cursor configures its triggers, instructions and tools. Cloud agents can also be kicked off conversationally from Slack (@cursor), PR comments, Linear, or the API with a text prompt. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation, and evidence that product settings beyond automations can be changed through natural language.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Cursor CLI lets you interact with AI agents directly from your terminal to write, review, and modify code.
The `/automate` skill lets you describe the workflow you want in plain language. Cursor configures the automation's triggers, instructions, and tools for you.
